{"task": {"id": "I_kwDONElfw88AAAABWIfHaQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlV6Pzg_r23c", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlV6P", "number": 45, "title": "Prepare first public npm release as @takahirox/three-mmd", "body": "## Goal

Prepare the **first public npm release** of this project under the agreed package name **`@takahirox/three-mmd`** so users can install it normally:

```sh
npm install @takahirox/three-mmd three@~0.186.0
```

Consumers must be able to use the loader, animation/physics, TSL materials, outlines, and existing VPD exporter from the scoped package. This name is intended to remain appropriate when future exporter functionality is added.

**Scope: rename and release preparation of the npm package only.** Keep the GitHub repository as `takahirox/three-mmd-loader` for now. Do **not** rename the repository or change the existing GitHub Pages address `https://takahirox.github.io/three-mmd-loader/` in this Issue. Any repository rename is a separate future decision.

## Motivation

The unscoped npm name `three-mmd-loader` belongs to a different package/publisher. This project must **not** publish to or direct users to install that unrelated unscoped package. Use the maintainer's scope `@takahirox/three-mmd` exclusively, subject to normal npm account/scope publishing permissions. The current checked-in `package.json` still uses `"name": "three-mmd-loader"`, version `0.1.0`, and `mmd-parser ^1.1.4`; it already builds ESM JS and TypeScript declarations with a root export and documented .js subpaths.

## Implementation

- Set `package.json` `name` to **`@takahirox/three-mmd`**, synchronize `package-lock.json` root/package metadata and other package-self references; preserve current supported Three.js peer version `~0.186.0` and `mmd-parser ^1.1.4` runtime dependency unless a concrete issue requires otherwise.
- Configure **public scoped npm publishing** via `publishConfig.access: "public"` and the appropriate registry; do not enable automatic publish from Actions, commit npm tokens, or require repository secrets.
- Maintain one-command **manual maintainer `npm publish`** from a clean, checked-out default branch. Set up lifecycle checks as needed so that the command itself builds the package, checks types and runs relevant automated offline/package verification before publishing, following the existing `mmd-parser` release approach. Document npm login, scope ownership and npm 2FA/token requirements as *manual maintainer prerequisites*; never claim that the agent can perform these account actions.
- Rewrite public installation instructions, root imports, addon-style subpath examples, TS documentation, package self-imports and consumers to the scoped name. Keep the actual exported symbols (`MMDLoader`, `MMDExporter`, `MMDAnimationHelper`, etc.) and stable subpath structures.
- Update repository-local examples, private viewer import maps and source imports/test fixtures from the old package specifier to **`@takahirox/three-mmd`**. Their URLs must still resolve to checkout-built `dist/` modules so local/Pages examples do not require the package to have been published first. Keep existing public example content/models/screenshots/asset manifest and Pages URL unchanged.
- Update release-facing project identity/metadata (npm README/package description/keywords/repository/homepage/issues links where useful) without misrepresenting current export capabilities: `MMDExporter` currently exports **VPD**, not full PMD/PMX/VMD. Do not implement a new exporter in this Issue.
- Include the existing `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and published runtime JS/TS declarations. Keep all third-party PMX/VMD, private test models, README/licenses of downloaded models, dev viewer files, test fixtures, CI artifacts, tokens, and generated example assets outside the npm tarball.
- Scope/name availability and authorization must be checked against **public npm** when reachable. Differentiate 404 (no release), permissions/ownership errors, network/DNS issues and stale registry caching. Do not assert that `@takahirox/three-mmd` is available or published unless independently verified. If npm account/scope authorization is missing, prepare all changes and state the exact maintainer action required; **do not publish to a fallback name**.

## Fully automated pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] `package.json`, lockfile and all user-facing package installation and import examples consistently use exactly `@takahirox/three-mmd`; no active unscoped `three-mmd-loader` package imports remain. Historical GitHub repo URLs and Pages paths are intentionally unchanged.
- [ ] `npm ci`, package build, strict TS checks and existing Node/browser test suites pass; current addon functionality and public APIs remain unchanged.
- [ ] `npm pack --dry-run` and `npm publish --dry-run --access public` pass without actually publishing. Verify package name/version, public access and tarball contents, including the root and all supported `.js` export subpaths and `.d.ts` files.
- [ ] Isolated **tarball-installed** JS (ESM) and strict TypeScript consumer tests import both package root and all documented subpaths via `@takahirox/three-mmd`; no local build path/source alias or unpublished registry package is needed to pass.
- [ ] The `npm publish` lifecycle runs required build/typecheck and offline/package regression gates automatically, is deterministic/repeatable, and does not publish if any gate fails. `npm publish --dry-run` must exercise appropriate prepublish checks without uploading a package.
- [ ] Local browser examples and private viewer resolve the renamed import maps and remain functional before any npm release. Mandatory WebGL2, native WebGPU when available, and browser/example integration regressions pass.
- [ ] `MMD_EXAMPLE_FIXTURES=1 npm run build:examples` plus `npm run test:examples` work without fetching licensed private assets. Generated fixture output is only for validation and **must not** be deployed as the live examples.
- [ ] Publishing artifacts exclude `examples/assets/`, `local-viewer/`, `scripts/`, private/downloaded model caches, test assets, archives and any credentials. Public examples' existing model, VMD, screenshots, asset catalog, live URLs and Pages deployment behavior are unchanged.
- [ ] Reproduce the intended consumer instructions: `npm install @takahirox/three-mmd three@~0.186.0` **after** the maintainer publishes. Before publication, verify via local packed tarball rather than falsely claiming it is already in npm.
- [ ] All tests, pack and publish dry-runs are pre-merge; no human login, npm publication, live Pages validation or post-merge verification is required to complete this implementation Issue/PR.

## Release operation (separate maintainer step, not a merge gate)

Once the changes merge and the maintainer's `@takahirox` npm scope is authorized:

```sh
npm publish
```

The package is published publicly under **`@takahirox/three-mmd`**. This issue prepares the command but **does not publish** the package, provision npm identity/2FA or verify post-publication availability as part of Issue/PR completion. Future releases can use the same simple command after changing the version.

## Required post-merge verification

**None** for this Issue/PR. The npm publish itself is an explicitly separate manual release step.
